thread:
maria: Quick heads-up — Helix POC reporting high first-response latency (600-900ms) on short prompts (~12-30 tokens). Using hosted rw-instruct-13b-8k in us-west-2. They said they turned on client prefetch/prefill (prefill_tokens=5) but traces don't show warmup hits. Can we swarm? They want a mitigation and rough cost impact before next call.

devon: Can you paste an example request + headers? Also are they streaming? Prefill behavior differs for streaming vs non-streaming.

maria: Sample below (they're using non-streaming):

maria: ```bash
curl -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <key>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{\"model\":\"rw-instruct-13b-8k\",\"input\":\"Summarize: ...\",\"prefill_tokens\":5,\"stream\":false}'
```

maria: They also added header `X-Client-Intent: low-latency` from the SDK.

devon: OK. Two quick checks: 1) confirm server saw prefill flag (we log x-prefill in request attrs), 2) check KV cache miss ratio for that model and shard. If prefill isn't recorded server-side, it's a client-side param only and won't warm kernel cache.

kai: I'm on infra. Looking at recent telemetry from that customer: high fraction of batches size=1 for their traffic shape (p50 batch size = 1, p95 = 2). That explains CPU/latency overhead. No widespread 429s, but we see many short-lived sessions and KV cache_miss:true in the model logs for the majority of requests.

kai: Two actionable mitigations:
- Ask client to increase parallelism on their side (bundle multiple user requests into a single RPC) OR
- Enable server-side prefill routing (route config flag allow_server_prefill: true) so we can warm the KV/prefix on the first RPC we see for that session.

devon: Also check if they're using prefer_latency routing. prefer_latency disables some batching windows; if they have very bursty small requests, switching to prefer_throughput (or increasing batching delay to ~10-20ms) will allow batches to form and reduce per-request overhead.

maria: Customer is worried about cost impact for prefill/warmup — can we quantify? They do ~120 reqs/min during demo peak.

ryan_support: Quick back-of-envelope: prefill_tokens=5 adds 5 input tokens billed per caller RPC. At 120 req/min that's 600 tokens/min -> 36k tokens/hr. At hosted price X per 1k input tokens (replace with plan rate) that's ~ (36k/1k)*X = 36*X per hour. For a 1-hour demo it's modest. Dedicated would reduce per-token compute egress overhead but has commit costs. I'll pull precise numbers from the account's pricing tier and DM.

devon: Also note that prefill helps TTFT only if the model/process memory warms (KV + fused-kernel paths). If batch sizes are 1, warming is largely wasted because the kernel startup dominates. So fix batching *first*, then prefill.

kai: I enabled a temporary canary server-side flag for the customer's route to allow server-side prefill and a small batching delay. Deploy-bot: "canary rollout: prefill-server-allow=true, batching_delay_ms=15 to 10% for route helix-demo"

deploy-bot: canary rollout started -> canary id c-2245 -> logs show route config applied.

kai: Early canary metrics: p50 TTFT dropped from 710ms -> 320ms, p95 from 920ms -> 540ms. Batch sizes increased p50=1 -> 2, p95=1 -> 3. KV cache hit ratio improved from 12% -> 46% in canary.

maria: Nice. Customer asks: if we recommend turning this on permanently, will it change billing or SLA? They also want a one-page note we can share with procurement about cost vs SLA tradeoffs.

ryan_support: Billing: enabling server-side prefill doesn't change our billing semantics — tokens still billed as usual. If we recommend Dedicated to guarantee lower p95 and predictable latency, that'll be a contract change (monthly commit). I'll draft an email comparing the two options (hosted + prefill tweaks vs Dedicated reserved capacity) with expected p95 numbers and estimated extra token spend.

devon: For short-term POC runbook:
1) Keep prefill_tokens=5 client-side.
2) Ask client to set SDK option batching_delay_ms=10 (if available) or set X-Redwood-Batching-Delay: 15 header.
3) We'll keep server-side canary for 24h and monitor p95.
4) If stable, promote canary and create a config note for the account.

maria: I'll relay steps to Helix and schedule a quick call in 30m. Can someone own the post-call follow-up with metrics and the procurement note?

ryan_support: I'll own the procurement note and cost numbers.

kai: I'll keep the canary running and post an update in 1h. If we see any regression, I'll roll back.

maria: Thanks all — will update after the call. :thumbsup: 

kai: quick note — if anyone needs raw logs for the session, ping me and I'll export model logs and prefix cache traces.

maria: Pinged Helix with instructions. Call in 25m.
